conv: D8. single: running-campaign problem
message: client says cost per hire doubled this month and nothing changed on their side, what do i tell them

response.answer: When a client experiences a sudden cost spike without making any changes on their end, explain that job boards and publishers (like Indeed) control the bidding dynamics behind the scenes. Publishers often raise their CPCs—especially towards the end of a month or quarter—to capture more spend. Even if you receive a similar volume of clicks or traffic, higher CPCs directly drive up your CPAs and cost per hire. Advise the client to look into the raw CPC trends to verify if publisher bid rates increased.
response.quote: where and that itself causes your CPAs to go up. Right? They give you the same amount of clicks, amount of traffic. But if you actually look at the data, it's just the CPCs that have gone up.
